chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from a number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from Yahya ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Abi Najran, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

"Whoever glorifies Allah after the obligatory prayer with the glorification of Fatimah (peace be upon her) one hundred times, and follows it with 'La ilaha illa Allah' (There is no god but Allah), Allah will forgive him."

key_terms.بِلَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ: With 'There is no god but Allah'
key_terms.تَسْبِيحَ فَاطِمَ: The glorification of Fatimah (a specific dhikr formula)

ai.seo_question: What is the Tasbihat Fatimah and how is it performed after prayer?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith prescribes the recitation of 'Tasbihat Fatimah'—glorifications attributed to the Prophet’s daughter—after each obligatory prayer, linking this specific dhikr to the promise of divine forgiveness. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on the intercessory and exemplary role of Ahl al-Bayt in daily worship, transforming routine post-prayer rituals into a means of spiritual purification and grace.
